title: Preclinical Repurposing of Sitagliptin as a Drug Candidate for Colorectal Cancer by Targeting CD24/CTNNB1/SOX4-Centered Signaling Hub.
authors: Shih, Jing-Wen; Wu, Alexander T H; Mokgautsi, Ntlotlang; Wei, Po-Li; Huang, Yan-Jiun
one_liner_zh: 该文通过生物信息学与分子对接研究西格列汀靶向CD24/SOX4信号轴治疗结直肠癌，虽涉及分子对接但核心为药物重定位与肿瘤信号通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制研究。
abstract: Despite significant advances in treatment modalities, colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a poorly understood and highly lethal malignancy worldwide. Cancer stem cells (CSCs) and the tumor microenvironment (TME) have been shown to play critical roles in initiating and promoting CRC progression, metastasis, and treatment resistance. Therefore, a better understanding of the underlying mechanisms contributing to the generation and maintenance of CSCs is crucial to developing CSC-specific therapeutics and improving the current standard of care for CRC patients. To this end, we used a bioinformatics approach to identify increased CD24/SOX4 expression in CRC samples associated with poor prognosis. We also discovered a novel population of tumor-infiltrating CD24+ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), suggesting that the CD24/SOX4-centered signaling hub could be a potential therapeutic target. Pathway networking analysis revealed a connection between the CD24/SOX4-centered signaling, beta-catenin, and DPP4. Emerging evidence indicates that DPP4 plays a role in CRC initiation and progression, implicating its involvement in generating CSCs. Based on these bioinformatics data, we investigated whether sitagliptin, a DPP4 inhibitor and diabetic drug, could be repurposed to inhibit colon CSCs. Using a molecular docking approach, we demonstrated that sitagliptin targeted CD24/SOX4-centered signaling molecules with high affinity. In vitro experimental data showed that sitagliptin treatment suppressed CRC tumorigenic properties and worked in synergy with 5FU and this study thus provided preclinical evidence to support the alternative use of sitagliptin for treating CRC.
abstract_zh: 尽管治疗手段取得了显著进展，结直肠癌（CRC）仍是一种在全球范围内理解不足且高度致命的恶性肿瘤。癌症干细胞（CSCs）和肿瘤微环境（TME）已被证明在启动和促进CRC进展、转移及治疗耐药中发挥关键作用。因此，更深入地理解CSCs产生和维持的潜在机制，对于开发针对CSCs的特异性疗法及改善CRC患者当前标准治疗至关重要。为此，我们采用生物信息学方法，在CRC样本中识别出与不良预后相关的CD24/SOX4表达升高。我们还发现了一种新的肿瘤浸润性CD24+癌症相关成纤维细胞（CAFs）群体，提示以CD24/SOX4为中心的信号枢纽可能是一个潜在的治疗靶点。通路网络分析揭示了CD24/SOX4中心信号、β-catenin和DPP4之间的关联。新兴证据表明，DPP4在CRC发生和进展中发挥作用，暗示其参与CSCs的产生。基于这些生物信息学数据，我们研究了西格列汀（一种DPP4抑制剂和糖尿病药物）是否可被重新利用以抑制结肠CSCs。通过分子对接方法，我们证明西格列汀以高亲和力靶向CD24/SOX4中心信号分子。体外实验数据显示，西格列汀处理抑制了CRC的致瘤特性，并与5FU协同作用，本研究因此为西格列汀治疗CRC的替代用途提供了临床前证据。
